`priority:p3`: a `surface` sentence in a ledger entry, whose only readers are `objectstack migrate meta` and the upgrade guide. ⚠️ **But those readers are exactly the ones a customer meets during an upgrade** — which is why it is p3 rather than nothing.

The blocker closed, so this card was an unlock candidate. It failed the second release double-check — and chasing that failure is what found the work already done.

**① Condition, from the most recent conversion comment (`5626876612`):** `Blocked-by: #16099`, deliberately naming the issue rather than PR #17559. Measured: **#16099 is `closed` / `completed`** (2026-09-10T23:44:35Z) and **PR #17559 is MERGED** (2026-09-10T23:44:33Z). ⇒ condition met.

**② Refused-if-newer check: FAILED, and correctly so.** The timeline carries a merged PR newer than the conversion comment (#17567, merged 2026-09-11T02:44:03Z). Per 「放行双查」② — 「refuse to release when the card carries a MERGED PR newer than that conversion comment (the card moved on after the condition was written, so the cited fact can be true and no longer current)」 — the release was refused and the premise re-measured instead. ⭐ Had it been released on the blocker's closure alone, this card would have gone back into the dispatch queue carrying work that is finished.

## The re-measurement — the same field, read at two commits

**At `ad715aca5`, the sha this card states it measured (`registry.ts:6491-6497`):**

> ⛔ The compile leg is scoped to that class and to nothing else: the table's string rows are under #16785 (ruled C — the table itself is to be amended to accept `min` / `max` over them) and its `sum` × `percent` row is not executed here either, **so no non-temporal pair changes behaviour**

**On `origin/main` `1bdbf82cb5` now (`registry.ts:6745-6753`), the same `surface` field:**

> ⚠️ This entry is ONE OF TWO on this leg, and its scope sentence is kept as written: it covered the temporal class and nothing else when it was registered. The non-temporal `sum` / `avg` rows followed under **#16099**, which registered NO entry of its own — it declared `not-required (already-registered dataset-measure-aggregate-field-type-refused)` against THIS id — so its widening rides this entry's prescription rather than a separate one. The `min` / `max` rows over every class the table refuses are the second entry, `dataset-measure-selecting-aggregate-field-type-refused` (**#17560**). ⇒ Read BOTH when migrating; there is no third

⇒ **Item 1 discharged.** The false final clause is gone, and what replaced it states the true relationship rather than merely deleting the falsehood.
⇒ **Item 2 discharged.** The card also asked, since the text was being touched, that the dangling **#16785** citation be corrected. It is no longer in the entry. Instrument check: `#16785` in `registry.ts` → **0**; control `#16099` / `#17513` in the same file with the same call → **4**. The instrument is lit, so the zero is a real absence.

⚠️ **One honest note about method, because it nearly went the other way.** A single-line `git grep` for the clause returns 0 on `origin/main` — but that zero proves nothing here: this `surface` value is built from `'…' + '…'` fragments, so the phrase spans a concatenation boundary and no single-line pattern could ever match it, at either sha. Per 「跨行短语配跨行控制词」 the grep was discarded. **The load-bearing evidence is the direct read of the whole field at both commits, quoted above** — not the grep.

First observed carrying the new wording at `e6965dd7ee`. ⚠️ Stated as an observation, ⛔ not an attribution: that commit's squash title names an unrelated card, so which PR authored the rewrite is not established here and this card does not need it.
